parent_objective: audit whether the single protected key window is saturated before more PPO

public_gates: compare protected-key normal-margin trajectory across M259 through M264
compare exact-source improvement versus remaining protected-key slack
separate replay or behavior regressions from protected-key window pressure
decide whether another PPO repeat is admissible
forbidden_shortcuts: do not run PPO in M265
do not loosen the protected key without recorded evidence
do not tune from private holdout evidence
do not start medium PPO until the audit decision is recorded
hypothesis: The M263 to M264 repaired stage2 path has nearly saturated the single protected-key normal-margin window, so more PPO should be blocked until the protected surface or gate policy is refreshed.
success_criteria: M265 records the protected-key normal-margin trajectory and remaining slack
M265 identifies whether the current blocker is protected-key saturation rather than replay, behavior, exact-source, or training instability
M265 records a concrete next milestone decision without running new PPO
failure_criteria: audit artifacts are insufficient to explain the protected-key alpha collapse
M265 starts new PPO or tunes from private holdout evidence

commands.name: m265_saturation_audit
commands.command: Summarize M259-M264 protected-key margins, source deltas, replay gates, and behavior gates into a no-training audit.

decision_rule: M265 does not promote a checkpoint. It must decide whether to refresh the protected surface, adjust the protected-key gate, add a stronger window-aware anchor, or admit another repaired stage2 repeat.
